neighbours.label: mixing up or confusing one thing for another by mistake ('mix up', 'got the dates confused', 'switched by accident'), as against literal mixing and blending
fire: My grandfather often mixes up the names of his grandchildren.
The clerk got the two files mixed up and sent the wrong letter.
It's easy to mix up the words 'affect' and 'effect' when writing fast.
The nurse accidentally swapped the labels on the two samples.
I always confuse the twins because they wear the same clothes.
Somehow the airline mixed up our bags and we got a stranger's suitcase.
Students often mix up latitude and longitude on the quiz.
He mistook his neighbour's car for his own and tried to unlock it.
quiet: My grandfather often mixes the paint himself before starting a canvas.
The baker got the two doughs mixed in a big steel bowl.
It's easy to mix cement and sand when you have the right tools.
The nurse carefully placed the labels on the two samples.
I always enjoy seeing the twins because they are so cheerful.
Somehow the band mixed jazz and folk into a single great album.
Students often mix colors in the art room on Fridays.
He washed his neighbour's car as well as his own on Sunday.
